name: Virtual power plant with revenue share for home batteries
summary: An aggregator pools many home batteries (and other flexible devices) into one controllable resource, sells grid services and market products, and shares part of the proceeds with owners.
how_it_makes_money: Revenue from grid services and energy trading, minus the share paid to asset owners and platform costs; the hardware seller can also earn on the battery sale or an electricity contract.

hardware: Home batteries or other flexible assets with remote control
sites_assets: Thousands of distributed assets in customer homes
partners: Trading partner or market access provider
regulation: Prequalification for balancing and reserve markets
financing: Hardware financed by customer, provider or a bundled contract
channel: Bundled with battery sale and electricity contract

stakeholder_value.customer: Share of VPP proceeds, often via an electricity contract

what_must_be_true: Enough assets are pooled to qualify for market products
Market prices leave a margin after the owner share and platform cost
Customers keep their devices online and allow remote control
Rules allow small assets to participate

risks_failure_causes.text: Per-household revenue figures in public sources are small and vary widely, from tens to a few hundred euros per year
Revenue depends on market prices and product rules that can change
Requires reliable internet connection and compatible hardware
The pioneer aggregator sonnen filed for insolvency in October 2026, two months after Shell sold it; services for customers continue

cases.note: Launched SonnenFlat in 2019 sharing VPP proceeds with owners. By 2023 its VPP had 250 MWh with a target of 1 GWh in the following years, providing frequency containment reserve and exchange trading.
Sonnen handles the connection of storage units while marketing and activation of reserve are done through Next Kraftwerke.

Sold by Shell to investor TIVEN in August 2026 and filed for insolvency about two months later, as reported by Handelsblatt via energy-storage.news. Cost cuts did not reach targets. The VPP business of the company was an early mover and customer services continue. The cause is not stated beyond that.
